title: Spark's entire non-mainnet footprint is provisioned but ceiling-suppressed
content:
Across the two non-mainnet subtrees in this chunk, every conduit with populated limits sets both ceilings to zero while keeping a regeneration rate. Base Fluid sUSDS: inflow "`maxAmount`: 0, `slope`: 5,000,000 per day", outflow "`maxAmount`: 0, `slope`: 5,000,000 fsUSDS per day" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.2.2.1.2.4.1/.2). Base Aave USDC: inflow 0 with a 25,000,000 per day slope, outflow 0 with slope Unlimited (.2.3.1.2.4.1/.2). Arbitrum Fluid: identical to Base Fluid (.3.1.1.2.4.1/.2). Arbitrum Aave USDC: 0 with a 50,000,000 per day slope (.3.2.1.2.4.1/.2).

The one exception is the Base Morpho vault, whose inflow figures are populated — and malformed.

Individually each of these is the paused-conduit configuration seen on mainnet. Collectively they say something larger: the cross-chain expansion exists as governance work rather than as deployed capital. Venues have been chosen, sized, given operational procedures and in several cases risk-reviewed, and none of them can currently move anything.

That is a coherent sequencing — approve and document the destination before routing capital to it, so that enabling a chain later is a parameter change rather than a fresh proposal. It also means any assessment of Spark's multichain risk from this Artifact must read the ceilings, not the instance count. Four chains and a dozen documents describe a footprint whose current exposure, as configured, is zero everywhere outside Ethereum.
